descriptionChirho: Exclamatory interjection expressing astonishment, grief, or lamentation, characteristically opening the book of Lamentations. Translated as 'how' (eng), '¿cómo / ¡Cómo!' (spa), 'कैसे' (hin), 'كَيْفَ' (arb), '어떻게 / 어찌하여' (kor), 'Jinsi gani' (swa). Used rhetorically to bewail a devastating reversal or calamity, not seeking literal information.

Interrogative interjection asking about location or place, semantically distinct from the exclamatory 'how' sense. Translated as 'where' (eng), 'dónde' (spa), 'कहाँ' (hin), 'أِيكَه' (arb), '어디서' (kor), 'wapi' (swa). The Arabic notably preserves a distinct transliteration أِيكَه reflecting the locative force rather than modal كَيْفَ.
